The demonstration realized several benefits of robotic (mechanical) fueling, including: • Robot can be precise • Robot will not drop and damage the nozzle • Higher precision robot leads to less reduced wear and tear between components • Less Hose flexing/twisting • No human contact with -40°C fueling components during fueling Conceptual operations for fueling on-road vehicles NREL completed the concept and specification review for automotive fueling. A flow chart of processes is shown in Figure 30. An analysis of the autonomous system operation codes that should be considered in the design of such a system are in Figure 31. Figure 32 shows a comparison of the potential for an autonomous system to drastically reduce fueling times versus a human operator. Figure 30: Example flowcharts for automotive fueling. The finding of this study is that robotic fueling for on road vehicles can be initiated in 9 seconds vs the 77 seconds needed for a human operator.
